newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Fuel Oil - Well supported though talks thin.
newsitem.headline: Asia Fuel Oil - Well supported though talks thin.

text.p: Singapore's high sulphur fuel oil market was quiet on Wednesday ahead of the May Day holiday but traders said they expected prices to firm in the near term amid crude strength and fewer exports from the Middle East.
A 380-cst grade cargo was heard offered at $91.50 per tonne, up from Monday's $91.00 trading level for late May lifting, but there were no buyers, traders said.
On Monday, one 20,000 tonne 180-cst grade cargo traded at $98.50 per tonne.
"Prices will not jump significantly as demand is not great at the moment, but they should be well supported," said one trader.
The trader said he expected prices for the 180-cst grade to move toward the $100 per tonne level after the holiday.

Trade on the SIMEX futures contract firmed in line with crude gains on late Wednesday with more than 90 lots exchanged hands. June futures edged 50 cents up to $98.50 and July advanced 60 cents to $98.50.
Fuel oil swaps also rose, with May at $98.75/$99.50 and June at $97.50/$98.00, compared with $98.25/$99.00 and $97.25/$98.00, respectively, on Tuesday.

The physical market was little affected after Singapore's Trade Development Board (TDB) released the Singapore weekly residues stocks, which fell by 162,000 barrels to 10.431 million barrels for the week ending April 29.
"The weekly stocks just came back to the normal level," said one trader.
But most traders noted summer demand in Kuwait would lead to fewer exports to Asia, tightening supplies.

Sentiment in the LSWR market remained bearish amid ample supplies in May when Indonesia's Pertamina is scheduled to allocate 3.85 million barrels and an additional 500,000 barrels will be rolled over from April.
